clue.text: Cowardly fellow stopped being elegant

indicators.note: the fellow is stopped from appearing, so his name is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: chicken is slang for cowardly, as in 'too chicken to try'
Ken is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A coward stopped trying to look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped' removes KEN from CHICKEN, leaving the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes a stylish, fashionable look, so being chic is being elegant.

clue.text: Wagnerian singer accommodated short number in record

parts.note: to accommodate a crowd is to hold it, past tense held

indicators.note: the short number goes inside the word for record

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
No. is the usual short form of number

explanation.surface: An opera singer found room for a brief tune on an album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a noun (a disc) but is the verb, to log or note down. A heldentenor is the heroic tenor voice of Wagner's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: German for 'heroic tenor', the voice type written for Wagner's leading men such as Siegfried.

clue.text: Trusted friend, and fell into outburst of rage after scam

indicators.note: the outburst piece comes after the scam in the answer

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the outburst

parts.note: a fit of temper is an outburst of rage

indicators.note: fell in its old sense of fierce or savage treats the letters of 'and' roughly, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A friend lost their temper after being swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' is the old adjective meaning fierce or cruel, rearranging the word beside it, rather than the verb of falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidant is a person you trust with secrets, a close and trusted friend.

clue.text: I'm so stingy somehow, and I hate women

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A mean man confesses he is both tight-fisted and contemptuous of women.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a self-description: someone who says 'I hate women' is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogynist is a person who hates women, so the speaker's confession names one.

clue.text: Straw originally in service replaced by good floor covering

indicators.note: the letter from Straw in the service is swapped out for the one meaning good

parts.note: Mattins is the Anglican morning prayer service, spelt with two Ts in the Prayer Book

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word Straw

explanation.surface: Straw once used in church gave way to a better carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives S; 'replaced by' swaps the S of MATTINS for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Matting is coarse woven material such as rush or coir laid on floors, a floor covering.

clue.text: Develop abilities fully as a high-flyer would?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for using all your talents and trying new things
literally, a bird that flies high stretches out its wings

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of stretching out to fly means developing your talents fully; literally it is what a bird does.

clue.text: Managed to break into US city storehouse

indicators.note: the word for managed breaks into the city's name

parts.note: Gary is an industrial city in Indiana
to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in burgling a warehouse in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a building for storing grain, a kind of storehouse.

clue.text: Sugar preparation unwelcome on aircraft

definitions.meaning: the sweet sugar coating spread on cakes
ice forming on wings is a danger to aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: Icing is both a sugar coating for cakes and the build-up of ice on aircraft surfaces.

clue.text: See in Macbeth a nefarious noble

indicators.note: tells the solver to look for the answer inside the following words

explanation.surface: Look at the wicked aristocrat in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish lord or nobleman, the very title Macbeth held.

clue.text: Models with astronomical overheads, perhaps?

parts.note: overheads sounds like huge running costs, but these are buildings whose ceilings show projected stars and planets

explanation.definitionFit: Planetaria are domed buildings projecting models of the night sky onto the ceiling overhead.

clue.text: Endorsement one's required to enter Atlantic state

indicators.note: the letters for one's go into the state's abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state on the Atlantic coast
one's is read as I'S, I being the Roman numeral one and 's standing for is

explanation.surface: Travellers need an approval stamp to get into an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement in a passport permitting entry to a country.

clue.text: Twins, for example, returning skirt

indicators.note: returning says the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt

explanation.surface: Twins, say, going back to wearing short skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the sign of the zodiac, is represented by the twins Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: Spread a glue on a type of watch

indicators.note: spread as in spread out or scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for applying adhesive to a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogue watch shows time with hands on a dial rather than digits.

clue.text: Subscriber not intended to have right restricted

indicators.note: the word for not intended restricts, or confines, the R within it

parts.note: undesigned means not planned or not intended

explanation.surface: Someone signing up did not mean to have their rights curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' puts R inside UNDESIGNED after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The undersigned is the person who has signed below, i.e. subscribed their name to a document.

clue.text: Tailless creature in ancient portico

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off the animal

parts.note: a stoat is a small weasel-like creature

explanation.surface: An animal with no tail found in a classical colonnade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Two old women, smugly virtuous

indicators.note: two says the word for an old woman is used twice

parts.note: goody, short for goodwife, was an old title for a married woman of humble rank

explanation.surface: A pair of elderly ladies who are rather self-righteous.
explanation.walkthrough: Goody here is the old title, as in Goody Proctor; it stands for a woman, plural 'women' covering both copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A goody-goody is someone ostentatiously well-behaved, so it describes being smugly virtuous.

clue.text: Subtle implications or blatant examples?

definitions.meaning: hints or connotations carried beneath the surface
read as two words, ..., i.e. open or blatant examples

explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle implied meanings; split as overt ones they are blatant examples, the opposite.

clue.text: Stricken elm seen in second part of serial

indicators.note: the disordered letters are seen inside the word for second

parts.note: an instant is a moment, a second

indicators.note: stricken as in struck down or afflicted, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A diseased elm tree appears in the second episode of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like an ordinal before 'part' but is a noun, a moment of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one part of a serial published or broadcast in sequence.

clue.text: Lamb starts on leaves on bush above plant

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first letters sit above the pen name
the starts of the next three words give their first letters

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A lamb begins nibbling leaves on a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts on' takes L, O, B from 'leaves on bush'; 'above' puts them over ELIA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden plant, often with blue flowers, used in hanging baskets.

clue.text: Sketchy note about university we translated into French

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the French word goes round the university letter

parts.note: the French word for we is nous

explanation.surface: A vague memo about a university we rendered into French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places U after the N of NOUS, giving NUOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuous means slight or flimsy, as with a sketchy, thinly supported argument.

clue.text: Bring in container of coffee for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means the word is heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel for serving coffee or tea

explanation.surface: Fetch a coffee pot for the people watching the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic accent, where the R is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to bring it in, as income from work.

clue.text: Go from Mile End to Stratford East for weapon

definitions.text: Go from Mile End to Stratford East for weapon

parts.words: Go from Mile End to Stratford East for weapon
parts.note: travelling from Mile End to Stratford in East London takes you across the district of Bow, which lies between them

explanation.walkthrough: Mile End, Bow and Stratford are neighbouring districts in East London, so the journey means crossing Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow weapon firing bolts, made here from crossing Bow.

clue.text: Conservative possesses millions, causing rift

parts.note: to possess something is to have it, so he has
M is the abbreviation for million or millions

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's great wealth splits the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep gulf, and figuratively a profound division or rift.

clue.text: Start where filming takes place

definitions.meaning: the beginning or outset of something
read as two words, ..., the place where a film is shot

explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning; split as on set it is where filming happens.

clue.text: One fool turned in by another

indicators.note: by places the reversed word beside the second fool
turned says the little word is read backwards

parts.note: the word in is taken as written
another fool, here a twit

explanation.surface: One idiot is reported to the authorities by a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes IN into NI; 'another' means another fool, TWIT. 'turned in' suggests handing over to the police, but here it is a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or foolish person, one fool.

clue.text: Additional words written during extremely agreeable recess

indicators.note: the postscript is written in the middle of those letters
extremely points to the extreme, first and last, letters of agreeable

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is additional words at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A postscript added during a very pleasant holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a holiday or break but is an architectural alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess in a church, usually at the east end.

clue.text: Like a laird now involved in disembarkation

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the word for disembarkation

parts.note: a landing is the act of getting off a ship or aircraft

indicators.note: involved as in tangled or complicated, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Scottish estate owner is involved in a beach landing.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner, the owner of a landed estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate, so landowning describes him.

clue.text: Set of bones team dug up by saint's birthplace

indicators.note: dug up as in turned over like soil, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Tarsus, in modern Turkey, was the birthplace of St Paul

explanation.surface: Archaeologists unearth bones near the town where a saint was born.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsus is the group of five long bones in the foot between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Competing players expressed sadness vocally

indicators.note: vocally means as spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to sigh is to let out a breath expressing sadness, past tense sighed

explanation.surface: The players in the match let out sad sighs.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team, the group of players competing together.
